name: Ujamaa
summary: Ujamaa (Swahili for familyhood) is Julius Nyerere's African socialism: a society of mutual care and cooperation modelled on the traditional extended family, with no exploitation of one person by another. It puts land, banks and major industries under public and cooperative control, organises peasants into collective villages, relies on self-reliance rather than foreign aid or investment, and places power in a single party said to represent peasants and workers.
scope: Nyerere's Ujamaa as Tanzanian state doctrine from the 1962 essay through the 1967 Arusha Declaration and the 1973-75 villagization to its abandonment in the 1980s. It excludes other African socialisms (Nkrumah, Senghor, Touré) and Kwanzaa's later use of the term. The 1962 essay itself could not be opened in this session, so positions rest on the Arusha Declaration and reference works.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ujamaa aimed to wipe out poverty, ignorance and disease through the state, and Tanzania expanded free public health services in the villages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Arusha Declaration puts the main means of production under public and cooperative control and treats capitalist exploitation as the thing to be abolished.

public-ownership.rationale: The Declaration says banks, land, minerals and large industries should be owned by peasants through their Government and cooperatives, and banks and major industries were nationalised in 1967.

unions-good.rationale: Unions were folded into the party-led structure (the single-party state controlled worker bodies); Nyerere valued workers' welfare but not independent union power, and the sources say little.

property-fundamental.rationale: Land belongs to the nation, not to individuals, and the means of production are to be publicly owned; private property rights are subordinate to community needs.

cut-welfare.rationale: Ujamaa rests on mutual care within the community and state provision against poverty, so cutting welfare as dependency-creating is contrary to its ethic.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Declaration places ownership with peasants and workers through the state and cooperatives, and ujamaa villages were collective farms; direct firm-by-firm worker ownership was less stressed than public ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Tanzania's one-party state used preventive detention against perceived threats and the Declaration warns of internal stooges, but Ujamaa texts do not address counter-terrorism surveillance.

strong-leader.rationale: Nyerere ruled as a dominant president but the Declaration insists on democracy led by peasants and workers, and he stood down voluntarily in 1985; adherents are split on the value of a bypass-the-gridlock leader.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Declaration asks citizens to be ready to defend the nation and warns of internal stooges, but Nyerere's sources stress people's self-reliance more than larger security forces.

decide-locally.rationale: Ujamaa villages were meant to govern themselves through local participation, yet Tanzania was centralised under the party and villagization was imposed from above.

traditional-family.rationale: Ujamaa means familyhood and draws on the extended family as the model; the nuclear family was promoted, and women's roles were largely domestic.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Creed guarantees freedom of belief and equal treatment regardless of religion; Nyerere was Catholic but the state was officially secular, so there is no push for a larger religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ujamaa was anti-colonial, and Nyerere backed liberation movements against white-minority rule in southern Africa, so it supports redress of racial injustice, though domestic policy stressed racial equality rather than preference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ujamaa grounds itself in traditional African communal values and promoted Swahili as the national language, so preserving that heritage is part of the doctrine.

gradual-change.rationale: Ujamaa was a deliberate transformation: nationalisations in 1967 and mass villagization, rather than gradual respect for established institutions.

free-trade.rationale: The Declaration is suspicious of foreign investment and trade-dependence and insists independence means self-reliance, though not full autarky.

nation-first.rationale: Self-reliance puts national independence first, yet Nyerere strongly backed African unity and southern African liberation, so adherents split on putting country over cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Tanzania's 1978-79 war overthrew Idi Amin and Nyerere backed intervention against white-minority regimes; but he mostly framed anti-colonial solidarity, not a general right to intervene.

limit-growth.rationale: Ujamaa was a development ideology aiming to escape poverty through agricultural and later industrial growth, not an environmentalist limit on growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Declaration warns against over-reliance on modern industry and capital-intensive technology and puts hard work and people first.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ujamaa aimed at socialist transformation by constitutional party-led means rather than class revolution, yet Nyerere supported armed liberation struggles in southern Africa.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Declaration says government must be chosen and led by peasants and workers, and Nyerere feared an educated elite cut off from the people.

central-planning.rationale: The state controlled major industries and directed development plans, so a planned economy was accepted, though Ujamaa was built on peasant agriculture more than full command planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ujamaa accepted small-scale individual plots and cooperatives but not a developed market socialism; sources say little on markets between publicly owned firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Ujamaa treats land as national property rather than taxing its value; no support for Georgist single tax.

basic-income.rationale: Ujamaa insists everyone able should work, since in a socialist state all people are workers, which conflicts with an unconditional income.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state nationalised banks and major industries and directed national investment, and the party saw this as the way to build socialism.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land was national property worked collectively in villages, yet villagers kept household plots; concentrated property was rejected, but widely dispersed private ownership was not the goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ujamaa aimed at ending exploitation, not abolishing money; Tanzania had wages, taxes and a currency throughout.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The 1967 nationalisations brought banking under state control, the opposite of leaving money to the market. The sources concern commercial banks and do not discuss abolishing a central bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Ujamaa had party-aligned workers' and cooperative bodies but no developed doctrine of state-recognised bodies setting wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nyerere defended TANU as the sole party, representing peasants and workers, and the Arusha Declaration ties socialism to leadership by people who believe in it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Declaration rejects feudalism and demands leaders from among peasants and workers, and Tanzania became a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: The Declaration says socialism cannot exist without democracy, although Nyerere's democracy took the one-party, consensus form rather than the competitive multi-party form.

direct-votes.rationale: Ujamaa valued discussion in village assemblies, but the sources do not take a stand on referendums on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power rested in the party and the National Assembly, not in workers' councils, though villages had participatory committees.

right-to-secede.rationale: Tanzania, a union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, was built on national unity, and Nyerere pursued African federation rather than fragmentation.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Declaration demands that leaders be peasants or workers and rejects hierarchical feudalism, so innate fitness to rule is rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nyerere gave open support to armed liberation movements against colonial and white-minority rule, so he did not hold violence never justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Creed guarantees religious freedom and equality, while Nyerere himself was a Catholic; the state was officially secular without hostility to religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ujamaa derives from African communal traditions and socialist principles; the Creed guarantees freedom of belief and no religious basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Ujamaa put the economy and public life under state and party control, which rules out privatised courts, police and defence. The Arusha Declaration does not discuss this directly.

military-superiority.rationale: Tanzania's Declaration calls for readiness to defend the nation, but the doctrine stresses self-reliance and development over arms rivalry with other states.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Creed demands equality regardless of race, and Nyerere's Tanzania promoted a multiethnic nation unified through Swahili over tribalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Ujamaa rooted socialism in the classless harmony of traditional African society and denied that Africa had classes, in contrast to Marxist class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Ujamaa sought social and economic equality and ended discrimination, with leadership-code limits on salaries and incomes; equal outcomes is close to its aim.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial doctrine supports the claim in principle, but the Declaration rejects reliance on foreign gifts and stresses self-reliance over claims on former powers.

civilizational-union.rationale: Ujamaa strongly backed African unity based on continent, a form of shared-civilisation union, yet the doctrine is not about religion or civilisation in other senses.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ujamaa is defined by familyhood and the demand that no one exploit another; pursuit of self-interest is rejected as a capitalist attitude.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ujamaa stresses community over the individual and the duty of all to work, but the Creed also enumerates citizens' rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Ujamaa criticised heavy industrialisation but wanted development and prosperity, not rejection of industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Declaration cautions against emphasis on capital-intensive modern industry and stresses people and agriculture.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ujamaa draws on traditional communal values but seeks a modern socialist future, not restoration of a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Arusha Declaration puts belief in socialist principles first, even requiring that party members and leaders hold them.

direct-action.rationale: Ujamaa operated through the party and state and Arusha stresses government led by believers, not extra-parliamentary action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nyerere preached voluntary, participatory village socialism, but villagization was enforced from 1973-75; adherents split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Ujamaa aimed at agricultural and economic development to remove poverty, not a return to hunting and gathering.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communal sharing and mutual care underlie familyhood, but Ujamaa was a transitional socialism with work required, not a full communist distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: Public ownership aimed to end exploitation and serve peasants and workers rather than private profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Declaration defines socialism as a state in which no person exploits another and treats capitalism as exploitative.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ujamaa denied the Marxist class framework and sought democracy led by peasants and workers, not dictatorship over former classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Ujamaa villages were collective farms, voluntary at first and enforced in 1973-75, with household plots retained.

harm-principle.rationale: Ujamaa subordinated individual choice to community and party goals, so restrictions went beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Ujamaa emphasised community over the individual and collective ownership of land.

conscription.rationale: Nyerere introduced two years' compulsory national service for secondary graduates and the Declaration expects citizens to be ready to defend the nation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Ujamaa's democracy relies on participation and voice, and the Declaration treats self-reliance and staying in the community as basic.

state-as-business.rationale: The Arusha Declaration casts government as the servant of peasants and workers building socialism, not a firm with customers. It does not discuss this directly.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ujamaa held that freedom requires conditions such as escape from poverty, ignorance and disease, and stated economic equality as a goal.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Creed demands equal opportunity regardless of race, and Ujamaa's anti-colonial thought rejected racial hierarchies.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation ran through the party and elected National Assembly, not through families and trade bodies replacing parties.

total-state.rationale: The state dominated the economy and party was supreme, yet Ujamaa was not total control of culture and life and the Creed protects religion and expression.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ujamaa demanded transformation after colonialism but not a rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Tanzania defended its borders and Nyerere opposed expansion; Pan-African unity was meant to be voluntary.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Declaration rejects feudalism and wants leaders drawn from peasants and workers, which excludes rule by personal oaths. It does not address oaths of loyalty as such.

bound-labor.rationale: The Declaration rejects feudalism and says no one should live on the labour of others, which excludes serfdom. It does not address bound labour directly.

universal-morality.rationale: Ujamaa grounded its morality in African tradition while Nyerere was a Catholic; the sources give no stated view.

single-common-good.rationale: Ujamaa rests on consensus and a shared national purpose in which the community's welfare is the aim, not balancing group interests.

revive-national-language.rationale: Swahili was made the language of the state but it was already widely spoken, not a fallen-out-of-use language, so the item does not fit.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Declaration says socialism cannot exist without democracy and that the means of production should be controlled by the people they serve.

school-vouchers.rationale: Ujamaa's state-led education system (Education for Self-Reliance) opposes funding private school choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Ujamaa did not hold to balanced budgets, but the Declaration also warns against excessive dependence on borrowing from outside.

economic-freedom.rationale: Ujamaa put the means of production under public control and saw no threat to freedom in that, so it rejects the claim that political freedom needs private economic freedom. This follows from the Declaration's principles; it does not discuss the claim directly.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Declaration's Leadership Code relied on leaders living by socialist standards, but the state also used laws and detention.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial independence was Ujamaa's starting point and Nyerere led Tanganyika to independence.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Declaration says that in a socialist country all people are workers and only children, the old and disabled may live on others' work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Ujamaa denied class divisions in African society and sought cooperation in a national family, though the Declaration condemns capitalist exploitation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Ujamaa valued traditional African culture and heritage rather than sacrificing it for new creation.

dominated-front.rationale: Nyerere pursued African unity, liberation support and Third World solidarity against domination, though sources do not describe an anti-Western bloc as such.

workers-nation.rationale: Ujamaa was national in framing but also Pan-African and anti-imperialist; no stated view.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Ujamaa promoted the nuclear family and domestic roles in practice, but Nyerere also argued against women's subjugation, so adherents split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Creed demands equality regardless of race and Nyerere opposed apartheid.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Ujamaa denied the Marxist reading of classes in Africa; the sources do not provide a statement.

national-mission.rationale: The Declaration stresses Tanzania's own self-reliant path, and Nyerere did not promote spreading its system, though it inspired others in Africa.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Nyerere applied Mill to women's subjugation early, yet Ujamaa's women's organisation reinforced domestic roles, so the sources point both ways.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ujamaa had the state controlling the economy and providing social services.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Creed gives equality of opportunity regardless of race or religion and Ujamaa seeks equality among all.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Tanzania built socialism within one country and Ujamaa claimed an African path not dependent on world revolution.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Creed guarantees freedom of religious belief.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration says socialism requires democracy and a government chosen by peasants and workers.

population-transfer.rationale: Ujamaa villagization moved millions of peasants within Tanzania but not as ethnic expulsion; Nyerere's doctrine rejected ethnic discrimination.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Ujamaa uses the state's power to nationalise and compel, which contradicts a non-initiation principle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The state banned opposition, and the one-party framework supports defending the order, but no explicit statement exists.

vanguard-party.rationale: TANU was a mass party of peasants and workers with selective membership of believers, not a Leninist vanguard, so it is a partial fit.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Declaration is a policy for peasants and workers and aims at eliminating poverty, ignorance and disease.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The party-led state restricted independent strikes, though the Declaration does not address ballots.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Ujamaa attributed poverty to colonial exploitation and weak production and rejected the Malthusian view.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Tanzania's nation-building treated its ethnic diversity as compatible with unity through Swahili and equality.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The sources show elections within the single party, not lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The one-party state used preventive detention without trial against perceived threats.

party-controls-media.rationale: The state and party owned the main media in Tanzania, though the Creed promises freedom of expression.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The leadership code barred leaders from multiple salaries, house rental, and company directorships, and Nyerere took a modest salary cut.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Declaration requires members to accept party principles and be committed, implying binding discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nyerere pursued an East African federation and Pan-African unity, calling failure to create the federation his biggest failure.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Creed promises freedom of expression, yet the state controlled culture; no statement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nyerere served as president until voluntarily retiring in 1985 with periodic confirmation elections, indicating no limit was in place.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The leadership code barred leaders from renting houses to others but did not ban rental housing generally.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Declaration expects citizens to defend the nation and Tanzania built a people's militia, but the sources do not call for replacing the army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Declaration treats agriculture as the only road to development and warns town dwellers may exploit rural people; Ujamaa favoured village life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nyerere feared an educated elite cut off from the people and required national service of secondary graduates.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ujamaa revalued African traditions as equal to others against colonial hierarchy.

minority-language-support.rationale: Tanzania promoted Swahili as the unifying national language over ethnic languages.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Ujamaa put community above the individual.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Declaration states that independence means self-reliance and ties real freedom to transforming the economy.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The one-party state limited political freedoms in the name of development, but the Declaration insists democracy is needed for socialism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Declaration is sceptical of aid and insists on self-reliance; yet Nyerere accepted aid as a duty of rich states, so adherents are split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Tanzania held direct presidential elections with a single candidate, but no stated view exists.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land belongs to the nation and property exists to serve the whole population.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Creed calls for curbing excessive wealth, which conflicts with a flat tax favouring the rich.

character-from-environment.rationale: Ujamaa held that attitudes of mind such as capitalist acquisitiveness are social, and the party sought to build socialist citizens through education.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration requires that leaders live under the leadership code, and constrains them by principle.

leader-cult.rationale: Nyerere was honoured as Mwalimu, the Teacher, but sources on the doctrine do not endorse mass cult.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Ujamaa denied class struggle in traditional society and proposed cooperation, but the Declaration warned leaders could be corrupted.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Declaration treats land as national and Ujamaa moved farmers into villages instead of leaving estates, though estates were not the central issue.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Tanzania accepted colonial-era borders and Nyerere did not claim territory for co-nationals.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Creed guarantees freedom of religious belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Freedom of belief and equality of opportunity are in the Creed; no state dress code was part of Ujamaa.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: TANU's aims include African unity, and Nyerere pursued regional federations.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Ujamaa promoted a unified national culture over ethnic self-governing institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Ujamaa rejected Marxist stages thesis, holding that a peasant society could reach socialism without capitalism, though it stresses economic bases.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-reliance is a central doctrine of Arusha, although it did not fully close Tanzania off from trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Ujamaa relied on commitment to community and a leadership code instead of material rewards, and the village economy was premised on collective work.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Ujamaa was reformist through the party, though Nyerere backed liberation struggles.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Declaration rejects feudalism and requires leaders not tied to feudal privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ujamaa is an anti-colonial ideology that rejects colonial tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nyerere's education for self-reliance and national service aimed to build loyalty to the nation and its socialist aims.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Ujamaa treated capitalism as exploitative and inappropriate but made no claim about its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Self-reliance and anti-colonialism reject neocolonial dependence on the former colonial power.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Declaration stresses self-reliance and distrusts foreign investment but does not call for full delinking.

elective-rulers.rationale: Ujamaa required government chosen by peasants and workers, and rejected feudalism.

minority-veto.rationale: Ujamaa valued consensus discussion, but did not give a minority an absolute veto.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Ujamaa asks the better-off to share through familyhood, but it frames this as duty within the community, not aristocratic obligation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ujamaa demanded active participation in building socialism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Leadership Code was written to prevent leaders from becoming a privileged class, yet Ujamaa's own party claimed to represent the people, so adherents do not call the elite corrupt as such.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Nyerere was both head of state and party chairman, and the party led the state, so a head of state above party was not the model.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Declaration holds that independence means self-reliance and that aid and loans threaten it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Arusha Declaration treats poverty as the product of colonial and economic exploitation by richer states and urges self-reliance in response.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ujamaa is built on the claim that socialism grows from traditional African communal life and that African democracy and the one-party state differ from Western models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nyerere insisted on the supremacy of the party and civilian government over the army; a political guardian role for the military does not fit.

filial-duty.rationale: Ujamaa is modelled on the extended family with mutual obligation among its members, so care for parents follows from its core idea.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Ujamaa puts major industries and banks under public control and demands self-reliance rather than foreign investment, so foreign takeovers fit the opposite of its program.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Ujamaa put banks and insurance under public ownership and rejected private exploitation of workers, so private pension accounts contradict it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nyerere held that land belongs to the community and that a person has it only while using it, and the Arusha Declaration and villagization built on this.

single-official-language.rationale: Tanzania made Swahili the national language of government and schooling to unify the country, a policy Nyerere championed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: No stated position; Ujamaa aimed at equality but discussed class, not racial group outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Arusha Declaration criticises the pursuit of wealth and status and urges frugal living, with leaders barred from private wealth.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Ujamaa promoted large villages and family cooperation but the sources record no population-incentive policy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Ujamaa held that every able person should work and that the state should organise labour; Tanzania pursued full employment through villages and state firms, and the Declaration says all must work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Nyerere distrusted Western-led liberal order and backed a one-party state, so he would not see spreading multi-party democracy as the path to peace.

non-intervention.rationale: Nyerere championed national sovereignty and non-alignment, though Tanzania itself invaded Uganda in 1978-79 and backed anti-apartheid struggles, so the absolute form is not fully held.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Arusha creed insists on equality of all people regardless of race or religion and Nyerere stressed national unity.

local-production.rationale: Ujamaa villages aimed at local, collective production and self-reliance on local resources.

informal-organisation.rationale: Power rested in a single party (TANU/CCM) and village organisation was state-directed, not informal small groups.

religious-nation.rationale: The Declaration affirms freedom of worship and a secular state, and Nyerere's party deliberately united Muslims and Christians.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Arusha Declaration stresses independence, equality of peoples and self-reliance over dependence on powerful states.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Declaration puts the means of production in public hands while Ujamaa keeps personal property and the family household.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Declaration places major industries, banks and services under public and cooperative control.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Arusha Creed guarantees freedom of religion and Nyerere was a practising Catholic.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Declaration condemns capitalism as exploitation of man by man, in favour of socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ujamaa called for equality of women in the village economy, though gender roles remained traditional in practice.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ujamaa villages organised peasants into communal farming settlements, the core of the 1973-75 villagization.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ujamaa presents itself as a distinct African socialism, opposed to capitalism and to imported doctrinaire models.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nyerere's Tanzania was a one-party state and detained opponents, justified as unity and the party's representation of peasants and workers.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ujamaa arose from the anti-colonial struggle and rejects exploitation of one people by another.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Stressed village-level democracy and participation in development through ujamaa villages, though in a one-party framework.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nationalised banks and major industries under public control rather than relying on a market economy.

rich-first.rationale: The Arusha Declaration curbs excessive wealth through its Leadership Code and sets out that no one should exploit another.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ujamaa rejects inherited privilege and exploitation, and Nyerere led a one-party republic whose leaders were elected or chosen by the party, not inherited.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Declaration put major means of production under public control, treating private ownership of them as a source of exploitation; yet the party also restricted the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Nyerere's government governed through a party-state with preventive detention, while the Declaration and constitutions stressed law; adherents split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ujamaa was explicitly non-racial; the Arusha Declaration and Nyerere's policy opposed racial discrimination and extended citizenship to Tanzanians of all races.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Nyerere built a national identity that cut across religious and ethnic lines, and such boycotts contradict the familyhood principle.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Arusha Declaration condemns exploitation and the accumulation of private wealth and puts the major means of production under public control.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Ujamaa was framed as compatible with religion and Nyerere was a practising Catholic; the state did not promote atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Ujamaa relied on a strong single-party state with its own security organs and preventive detention, and no abolition was ever proposed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Ujamaa made the state and cooperative villages responsible for ending poverty and distrusted private charity and foreign aid as a route to dependence.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Self-reliance and independence are central, and Tanzania under Nyerere pursued non-alignment and was wary of foreign dependence.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Arusha Declaration says that in a socialist country every able person works, every worker gets a just return, and no one lives on the work of others.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nyerere supported armed liberation struggles and the Declaration speaks of revolution against exploitation, so adherents do not treat killing as always wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ujamaa draws on traditional African family life but Tanzania was a new multi-ethnic nation built on a single party, not a claim of ancient national continuity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Declaration frames politics as the work of building a socialist state on material and organisational terms, not as a spiritual struggle.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Declaration directs politics to building a socialist state and economy; cultural renewal is not placed before it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Declaration puts the economy under peasants and workers through the state and cooperatives, defined by class rather than ethnic majority.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Arusha Declaration says socialism requires that peasants and workers control the means of production and the government.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Ujamaa put major services and industries under public control and aimed at free public health and education.

municipal-property.rationale: Ujamaa villages held land collectively, but major industry went to the national state, so the answer is split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Arusha Creed holds all human beings equal and TANU opposed racial discrimination, so organising by race is rejected.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nyerere stressed peace and self-reliance but also sent the army into Uganda in 1978-79; adherents are split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Nyerere's one-party state sought national unity and opposed tribal and religious divisions in politics.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Ujamaa stressed women's equal labor in villages, but not distinct values in public life; no stated position.

capital-controls.rationale: The Arusha Declaration put banks and major industries under state control and rejected reliance on foreign capital.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Declaration stresses self-reliance and condemns dependence on rich-country aid and investment, and Nyerere later pressed for a fairer international economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Ujamaa worked through TANU and the existing state, nationalising industry and banks, not smashing the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Ujamaa was a single state-directed blueprint of village collectivisation, though framed as an African path rather than a copy of others.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Declaration opens with the belief that all human beings are equal, which grounds its call for dignity and an end to exploitation.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Ujamaa was secular and tolerant of the faiths of Tanzanians but made no claim about religions sharing one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Ujamaa made peasant agriculture its core, with cooperative and collective villages, public control of banks and state marketing of produce in place of private traders and moneylenders.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Ujamaa promoted Swahili as the national language but never addressed naming of regional varieties.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ujamaa placed collective welfare above individual interests but never addressed the environment against liberty.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Arusha Creed commits TANU to equality of all citizens and freedom of religious belief, with no state-favoured interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Nyerere defended democracy as participation and discussion within one party rather than competition between parties, so competitive elections were not what defined it.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Arusha Declaration says every citizen has the right to take an equal part in government, and the creed declares all human beings equal.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Land is held in common and belongs to the nation, and individual claims to land as property are rejected in favour of communal use.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Nyerere stressed sovereignty and self-reliance but also opposed apartheid and colonial crimes; no stated position on such courts.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Ujamaa was itself a planned state and opposed capitalist restoration, but it did not take a stance on bureaucratic rule elsewhere.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: No stated position; Nyerere backed self-determination in colonies but did not address plebiscites generally.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Arusha creed rests on human dignity and the equality of persons, which leaves no room for killing without trial.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Ujamaa expanded free health and education to all villages rather than means-testing them.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ujamaa placed power in a single mass party, TANU, as the channel of the people's will, so parties were not bypassed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Arusha creed and TANU membership rules reject discrimination by religion and keep politics non-denominational.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Arusha Declaration places the major means of production under the control of peasants and workers and rejects foreign capital dependence.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The Arusha Declaration treats exploitation and excessive wealth as injustices to be curbed whatever their origin, so fairness is judged by outcomes and by whether wealth rests on others' labour.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The Arusha Declaration makes hard work the root of development and Ujamaa stressed that everyone must work, so work is valued in itself rather than something to minimise.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Ujamaa joined African nationalism and unity with a politics for peasants and workers, as the Creed and party membership rules show.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Ujamaa put major industries and banks under public control within a single-party state and rejected capitalist markets; the later market opening came after the Ujamaa period.

police-more-powers.rationale: The Declaration asks citizens to be ready to defend the nation and warns of internal stooges, but Nyerere's sources stress people's self-reliance more than larger security forces. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Public leaders should be barred from holding company shares, extra salaries or rental property.
missingStatements.rationale: The Arusha Resolution's leadership code forbids leaders to hold shares or directorships, receive two salaries or rent out houses.

missingStatements.text: A poor country should rely on its own resources for development rather than on foreign aid, loans or investment.
missingStatements.rationale: The Declaration holds that independence means self-reliance and that aid and loans threaten it.

notes: Villagization was voluntary until 1973 and compulsory afterwards, so answers on compulsion, collective farming and means-match-ends describe the doctrine and its practice together. Nyerere later accepted multi-party politics, which this profile does not represent.
